I will farm this year much like last year, but I will keep the rates a little tighter where I think I can save money without cutting yield. On 10.1 mu in Quzhou, with wheat-maize rotation and well irrigation, I do not farm by guesswork anymore. I look at whether the stand is strong, whether the soil can hold water, and what yield I am trying to reach. Wheat is my steady crop, so I will keep fertilizer enough to protect yield, especially nitrogen, and I will split it so I do not waste too much early. For maize after wheat, I will still feed it well because summer maize responds fast if water and fertilizer keep up, and losing maize yield is expensive. I have only 2 people in the household and some off-farm work, so I will favor rotary tillage and practical operations I can finish on time. I will use improved or hybrid seed, keep irrigation to the key stages, and I will not cut pesticide too much because one bad outbreak can cost more than the spray bill. I will aim for stable output first, then control cost second.
